sanskrit: tato 'paśyaṃ vasūn rudrān sādhyāṃś ca samarudgaṇān ādityān aśvinau caiva tān sarvān pratyapūjayam
english: Then I beheld the Vasus, the Rudras, the Sādhyas, along with the hosts of Maruts, the Ādityas, and the twin Aśvins — I paid reverence to all of them.

sanskrit: te māṃ vīryeṇa yaśasā tejasā ca balena ca astraiś cāpy anvajānanta saṃgrāmavijayena ca
english: They acknowledged me with regard to valour, fame, radiance, strength, mastery of weapons, and victory in battle.

sanskrit: praviśya tāṃ purīṃ ramyāṃ devagandharvasevitām devarājaṃ sahasrākṣam upātiṣṭhaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Entering that beautiful city attended by gods and gandharvas, I stood before the king of the gods, the thousand-eyed Indra, with folded hands.

sanskrit: dadāv ardhāsanaṃ prītaḥ śakro me dadatāṃ varaḥ bahumānāc ca gātrāṇi pasparśa mama vāsavaḥ
english: The gladdened Śakra, foremost among givers, offered me half his seat, and Vāsava touched my limbs out of great respect.

sanskrit: tatrāhaṃ devagandharvaiḥ sahito bhuridakṣiṇa astrārtham avasaṃ svarge kurvāṇo 'strāṇi bhārata
english: There, O Bharata, I dwelt in heaven in the company of the gods and gandharvas, richly rewarded, acquiring and practising the weapons.

sanskrit: viśvāvasoś ca me putraś citraseno 'bhavat sakhā sa ca gāndharvam akhilaṃ grāhayām āsa māṃ nṛpa
english: Citrasena, son of Viśvāvasu, became my friend, O king, and he caused me to learn the entire science of music and dance.

sanskrit: tato 'ham avasaṃ rājan gṛhītāstraḥ supūjitaḥ sukhaṃ śakrasya bhavane sarvakāmasamanvitaḥ
english: Then, O king, having obtained the weapons and being greatly honoured, I dwelt happily in the abode of Śakra, furnished with every desire.

sanskrit: śṛṇvan vai gītaśabdaṃ ca tūryaśabdaṃ ca puṣkalam paśyaṃś cāpsarasaḥ śreṣṭhā nṛtyamānāḥ paraṃtapa
english: O scorcher of foes, I heard the sounds of song and the full sounds of instruments, and I watched the foremost apsarases as they danced.

sanskrit: tat sarvam anavajñāya tathyaṃ vijjñāya bhārata atyarthaṃ pratigṛhyāham astreṣv eva vyavasthitaḥ
english: Without slighting any of it, recognising it all as real, O Bharata, I accepted those gifts with great pleasure and yet remained wholly devoted to the weapons.

sanskrit: tato 'tuṣyat sahasrākṣas tena kāmena me vibhuḥ evaṃ me vasato rājann eṣa kālo 'tyagād divi
english: Then the thousand-eyed all-powerful Indra was pleased with that resolution of mine. Thus, O king, this period of time passed for me while I dwelt in heaven.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kṛtāstram abhiviśvastam atha māṃ harivāhanaḥ saṃspṛśya mūrdhni pāṇibhyām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Arjuna said: Then Hari's charioteer, fully trusting that I had mastered the weapons, touched my head with both hands and spoke these words to me.

sanskrit: na tvam adya yudhā jetuṃ śakyaḥ suragaṇair api kiṃ punar mānuṣe loke mānuṣair akṛtātmabhiḥ aprameyo 'pradhṛṣyaś ca yuddheṣv apratimas tathā
english: "You cannot now be conquered in battle even by the hosts of the gods — how much less by unrefined men in the world of humans! Immeasurable, unconquerable, and matchless in battles, you are."

sanskrit: athābravīt punar devaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ astrayuddhe samo vīra na te kaś cid bhaviṣyati
english: Then the god spoke again, his hair bristling with delight: "In warfare with weapons, O hero, there will be none equal to you."

sanskrit: apramattaḥ sadā dakṣaḥ satyavādī jitendriyaḥ brahmaṇyaś cāstravic cāsi śūraś cāsi kurūdvaha
english: "You are ever vigilant, skilful, truthful in speech, one who has conquered the senses, devoted to the Brahmins, skilled in weapons, and you are a hero, O best of the Kurus."

sanskrit: astrāṇi samavāptāni tvayā daśa ca pañca ca pañcabhir vidhibhiḥ pārtha na tvayā vidyate samaḥ
english: "Fifteen weapons have been obtained by you, O Pārtha, through five methods of mastery — there is none equal to you."

sanskrit: prayogam upasaṃhāram āvṛttiṃ ca dhanaṃjaya prāyaścittaṃ ca vettha tvaṃ pratighātaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: "You know, O Dhanaṃjaya, the invocation, withdrawal, repeated application, expiation, and the complete counter of each weapon."

sanskrit: tava gurvarthakālo 'yam upapannaḥ paraṃtapa pratijānīṣva taṃ kartum ato vetsyāmy ahaṃ param
english: "The time to render service to your teacher has now come, O scorcher of foes. Promise to perform it — thereafter I shall know what further to do."

sanskrit: tato 'ham abruvaṃ rājan devarājam idaṃ vacaḥ viṣahyaṃ cen mayā kartuṃ kṛtam eva nibodha tat
english: Then I said to the king of the gods, O king, these words: "If it is within my power to do it, consider it already done."

sanskrit: tato mām abravīd rājan prahasya balavṛtrahā nāviṣahyaṃ tavādyāsti triṣu lokeṣu kiṃ cana
english: Then the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra spoke to me with a laugh, O king: "There is nothing in the three worlds that is beyond your power today."

sanskrit: nivātakavacā nāma dānavā mama śatravaḥ samudrakukṣim āśritya durge prativasanty uta
english: "The dānavas known as the Nivātakavacas, my enemies, dwell in a stronghold sheltered within the depths of the ocean."

sanskrit: tisraḥ koṭyaḥ samākhyātās tulyarūpabalaprabhāḥ tāṃs tatra jahi kaunteya gurvarthas te bhaviṣyati
english: "They are said to number thirty million, all equal in form, strength, and splendour. Slay them there, O son of Kuntī — that will be the service to your teacher."

sanskrit: tato mātalisaṃyuktaṃ mayūrasamaromabhiḥ hayair upetaṃ prādān me rathaṃ divyaṃ mahāprabham
english: Then he gave me a divine and greatly resplendent chariot yoked to horses whose manes resembled peacock feathers, with Mātali as charioteer.

sanskrit: babandha caiva me mūrdhni kirīṭam idam uttamam svarūpasadṛśaṃ caiva prādād aṅgavibhūṣaṇam
english: He also bound on my head this excellent diadem and gave me body ornaments befitting my own nature.

sanskrit: abhedyaṃ kavacaṃ cedaṃ sparśarūpavad uttamam ajarāṃ jyām imāṃ cāpi gāṇḍīve samayojayat
english: He gave me this impenetrable armour, excellent and pleasant to the touch, and fitted this undecaying bowstring onto the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāyām ahaṃ tena syandanena virājatā yenājayad devapatir baliṃ vairocaniṃ purā
english: Then I set out in that gleaming chariot with which the lord of the gods had formerly conquered Bali, son of Virocana.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sarva eva tena ghoṣeṇa bodhitaḥ manvānā devarājaṃ māṃ samājagmur viśāṃ pate dṛṣṭvā ca mām apṛcchanta kiṃ kariṣyasi phalguna
english: All the gods, awakened by that tumult and thinking it was the king of the gods, came together, O lord of the people. And seeing me they asked: "What will you do, O Phalguna?"

sanskrit: tān abruvaṃ yathābhūtam idaṃ kartāsmi saṃyuge nivātakavacānāṃ tu prasthitaṃ māṃ vadhaiṣiṇam nibodhata mahābhāgāḥ śivaṃ cāśāsta me 'naghāḥ
english: I told them truthfully: "Know that I am setting out to battle with the intent of slaying the Nivātakavacas, O greatly fortunate and sinless ones." And they blessed me with auspiciousness.

sanskrit: tuṣṭuvur māṃ prasannās te yathā devaṃ puraṃdaram rathenānena maghavā jitavāñ śambaraṃ yudhi namuciṃ balavṛtrau ca prahlādanarakāv api
english: Pleased, they extolled me as they would the god Puraṃdara: "With this very chariot Maghavan conquered Śambara in battle, and also Namuci, Bala, Vṛtra, Prahlāda, and Naraka."

sanskrit: bahūni ca sahasrāṇi prayutāny arbudāni ca rathenānena daityānāṃ jitavān maghavān yudhi
english: "And with this chariot Maghavan has conquered in battle many thousands, millions, and hundreds of millions of daityas."

sanskrit: tvam apy etena kaunteya nivātakavacān raṇe vijetā yudhi vikramya pureva maghavān vaśī
english: "You too, O son of Kuntī, shall conquer the Nivātakavacas in battle by your prowess with this chariot, even as the self-controlled Maghavan did of old."

sanskrit: ayaṃ ca śaṅkhapravaro yena jetāsi dānavān anena vijitā lokāḥ śakreṇāpi mahātmanā
english: "And this foremost of conches — with it you shall conquer the dānavas. With it the great-souled Śakra himself conquered the worlds."

sanskrit: pradīyamānaṃ devais tu devadattaṃ jalodbhavam pratyagṛhṇaṃ jayāyainaṃ stūyamānas tadāmaraiḥ
english: The conch called Devadatta, born of the waters, given to me by the gods — I accepted it for victory, while being praised by the immortals at that time.

sanskrit: sa śaṅkhī kavacī bāṇī pragṛhītaśarāsanaḥ dānavālayam atyugraṃ prayāto 'smi yuyutsayā
english: Thus equipped with conch, armour, arrows, and bow in hand, I set out with the desire for battle toward the terrible abode of the dānavas.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca tato 'haṃ stūyamānas tu tatra tatra maharṣibhiḥ apaśyam udadhiṃ bhīmam apāṃpatim athāvyayam
english: Arjuna said: Thus being praised here and there by great sages, I then beheld the terrible, imperishable ocean, the lord of waters.

sanskrit: phenavatyaḥ prakīrṇāś ca saṃhatāś ca samucchritāḥ ūrmayaś cātra dṛśyante calanta iva parvatāḥ nāvaḥ sahasraśas tatra ratnapūrṇāḥ samantataḥ
english: Waves bearing foam, scattered and assembled, rising high, were seen there moving like mountains; and thousands of ships filled with jewels lay on all sides.

sanskrit: timiṃgilāḥ kacchapāś ca tathā timitimiṃgilāḥ makarāś cātra dṛśyante jale magnā ivādrayaḥ
english: Timiṃgilas, tortoises, and also timitimiṃgilas, and makaras were seen there, submerged in the water like mountains.

sanskrit: śaṅkhānāṃ ca sahasrāṇi magnāny apsu samantataḥ dṛśyante sma yathā rātrau tārās tanv abhrasaṃvṛtāḥ
english: Thousands of conches submerged all around in the water were seen like stars at night thinly veiled by clouds.

sanskrit: tathā sahasraśas tatra ratnasaṃghāḥ plavanty uta vāyuś ca ghūrṇate bhīmas tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Similarly, thousands of clusters of gems were floating there, and a terrible wind whirled — it seemed altogether wondrous.

sanskrit: tam atītya mahāvegaṃ sarvāmbhonidhim uttamam apaśyaṃ dānavākīrṇaṃ tad daityapuram antikāt
english: Having crossed that mighty, swiftly moving, supreme receptacle of all waters, I saw at close range that city of the daityas teeming with dānavas.

sanskrit: tatraiva mātalis tūrṇaṃ nipatya pṛthivītale nādayan rathaghoṣeṇa tat puraṃ samupādravat
english: Right there Mātali swiftly descended to the earth's surface and charged at that city, making it resound with the thundering of the chariot.

sanskrit: rathaghoṣaṃ tu taṃ śrutvā stanayitnor ivāmbare manvānā devarājaṃ māṃ saṃvignā dānavābhavan
english: Hearing that chariot's thunder as if it were a thunderclap in the sky, the dānavas were alarmed, thinking it was the king of the gods.

sanskrit: sarve saṃbhrāntamanasaḥ śaracāpadharāḥ sthitāḥ tathā śūlāsiparaśugadāmusalapāṇayaḥ
english: All stood with agitated minds, holding bows and arrows, as well as spears, swords, axes, clubs, and pestles in their hands.

sanskrit: tato dvārāṇi pidadhur dānavās trastacetasaḥ saṃvidhāya pure rakṣāṃ na sma kaś cana dṛśyate
english: Then the dānavas, their hearts struck with fear, shut the gates, having arranged the defence of the city — not one was to be seen outside.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkham upādāya devadattaṃ mahāsvanam puram āsuram āśliṣya prādhamaṃ taṃ śanair aham
english: Then, taking up the Devadatta conch of mighty sound and approaching the asura city, I blew it softly.

sanskrit: sa tu śabdo divaṃ stabdhvā pratiśabdam ajījanat vitresuś ca nililyuś ca bhūtāni sumahānty api
english: But that sound, filling the heavens, caused an echo to reverberate — even very great creatures trembled and hid themselves.

sanskrit: tato nivātakavacāḥ sarva eva samantataḥ daṃśitā vividhais trāṇair vividhāyudhapāṇayaḥ
english: Then all the Nivātakavacas on all sides, clad in armour of various kinds, weapons of various kinds in their hands,

sanskrit: āyasaiś ca mahāśūlair gadābhir musalair api paṭṭiśaiḥ karavālaiś ca rathacakraiś ca bhārata
english: with great iron spears, clubs, pestles, battle-axes, swords, and chariot wheels, O Bharata,

sanskrit: śataghnībhir bhuśuṇḍībhiḥ khaḍgaiś citraiḥ svalaṃkṛtaiḥ pragṛhītair diteḥ putrāḥ prādurāsan sahasraśaḥ
english: with śataghnīs, bhuśuṇḍīs, and variously adorned swords in hand — the sons of Diti appeared by the thousands.

sanskrit: tato vicārya bahudhā rathamārgeṣu tān hayān prācodayat same deśe mātalir bharatarṣabha
english: Then Mātali, having reflected much on the chariot-paths, urged the horses on level ground, O bull among Bharatas.

sanskrit: tena teṣāṃ praṇunnānām āśutvāc chīghragāminām nānvapaśyaṃ tadā kiṃ cit tan me 'dbhutam ivābhavat
english: By that swift driving of those swift-moving horses goaded forward, I could see nothing then — it seemed to me altogether wondrous.

sanskrit: tatas te dānavās tatra yodhavrātāny anekaśaḥ vikṛtasvararūpāṇi bhṛśaṃ sarvāṇy acodayan
english: Then the dānavas there urged on their many battalions of warriors, all of them of deformed voices and shapes, with great vigour.

sanskrit: tena śabdena mahatā samudre parvatopamāḥ āplavanta gataiḥ sattvair matsyāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: By that great noise, fish like mountains in the ocean, having lost their senses, leapt up by the hundreds of thousands.

sanskrit: tato vegena mahatā dānavā mām upādravan vimuñcantaḥ śitān bāṇāñ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Then the dānavas charged at me with great speed, releasing sharp arrows by the hundreds and thousands.

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāras tumulas teṣāṃ mama ca bhārata avartata mahāghoro nivātakavacāntakaḥ
english: That tumultuous battle between them and me, O Bharata, that great and terrible destruction of the Nivātakavacas, commenced.

sanskrit: tato devarṣayaś caiva dānavarṣigaṇāś ca ye brahmarṣayaś ca siddhāś ca samājagmur mahāmṛdhe
english: Then divine sages, groups of sages among the dānavas, brahmarṣis, and siddhas all came together for that great battle.

sanskrit: te vai mām anurūpābhir madhurābhir jayaiṣiṇaḥ astuvan munayo vāgbhir yathendraṃ tārakāmaye
english: Those sages, desiring my victory, praised me with fitting and sweet words, just as they had praised Indra in the battle against Tāraka.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca tato nivātakavacāḥ sarve vegena bhārata abhyadravan māṃ sahitāḥ pragṛhītāyudhā raṇe
english: Arjuna said: Then all the Nivātakavacas together rushed at me swiftly, O Bharata, weapons in hand for battle.

sanskrit: ācchidya rathapanthānam utkrośanto mahārathāḥ āvṛtya sarvatas te māṃ śaravarṣair avākiran
english: Those mighty warriors cut off the path of my chariot, screaming aloud, and surrounding me on all sides poured down showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tato 'pare mahāvīryāḥ śūlapaṭṭiśapāṇayaḥ śūlāni ca bhuśuṇḍīś ca mumucur dānavā mayi
english: Then other dānavas of great might, spears and battle-axes in hand, hurled spears and bhuśuṇḍīs at me.

sanskrit: tac chūlavarṣaṃ sumahad gadāśaktisamākulam aniśaṃ sṛjyamānaṃ tair apatan madrathopari
english: That very great shower of spears, mixed with clubs and śaktis, ceaselessly discharged by them, fell upon my chariot.

sanskrit: anye mām abhyadhāvanta nivātakavacā yudhi śitaśastrāyudhā raudrāḥ kālarūpāḥ prahāriṇaḥ
english: Other Nivātakavacas charged at me in battle, terrible strikers bearing sharp weapons and arms, their forms like death itself.

sanskrit: tān ahaṃ vividhair bāṇair vegavadbhir ajihmagaiḥ gāṇḍīvamuktair abhyaghnam ekaikaṃ daśabhir mṛdhe te kṛtā vimukhāḥ sarve matprayuktaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: I struck each of them with ten swift, straight-flying arrows released from the Gāṇḍīva in the battle — all of them were turned back by my stone-sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: tato mātalinā tūrṇaṃ hayās te saṃpracoditāḥ rathamārgād bahūṃs tatra vicerur vātaraṃhasaḥ susaṃyatā mātalinā prāmathnanta diteḥ sutān
english: Then those horses, swiftly urged on by Mātali, swift as the wind, coursed along many chariot-paths; well-controlled by Mātali they crushed the sons of Diti.

sanskrit: śataṃ śatās te harayas tasmin yuktā mahārathe tadā mātalinā yattā vyacarann alpakā iva
english: Those hundreds upon hundreds of horses yoked to that great chariot moved under Mātali's control as if they were but few.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ caraṇapātena rathanemisvanena ca mama bāṇanipātaiś ca hatās te śataśo 'surāḥ
english: By the trampling of their hooves, by the sound of the chariot's wheel-rims, and by the fall of my arrows, those asuras were slain by the hundreds.

sanskrit: gatāsavas tathā cānye pragṛhītaśarāsanāḥ hatasārathayas tatra vyakṛṣyanta turaṃgamaiḥ
english: Others, their lives gone, still clutching their bows, their charioteers slain, were dragged there by their horses.

sanskrit: te diśo vidiśaḥ sarvāḥ pratirudhya prahāriṇaḥ nighnanti vividhaiḥ śastrais tato me vyathitaṃ manaḥ
english: Those strikers, blocking all directions and intermediate directions, smote with various weapons — and then my mind was distressed.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ mātaler vīryam apaśyaṃ paramādbhutam aśvāṃs tathā vegavato yad ayatnād adhārayat
english: Then I saw Mātali's most wonderful prowess in the way he effortlessly controlled those swift horses.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ laghubhiś citrair astrais tān asurān raṇe sāyudhān acchinaṃ rājañ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Then with swift and varied weapons I cut down those asuras along with their arms in battle, O king, by the hundreds and thousands.

sanskrit: evaṃ me caratas tatra sarvayatnena śatruhan prītimān abhavad vīro mātaliḥ śakrasārathiḥ
english: As I moved about thus with all effort, O destroyer of enemies, the heroic Mātali, Śakra's charioteer, became pleased.

sanskrit: vadhyamānās tatas te tu hayais tena rathena ca agaman prakṣayaṃ ke cin nyavartanta tathāpare
english: Then those who were being slaughtered by the horses and that chariot went toward destruction — some, however, turned back.

sanskrit: spardhamānā ivāsmābhir nivātakavacā raṇe śaravarṣair mahadbhir māṃ samantāt pratyavārayan
english: The Nivātakavacas, as if competing with us in battle, surrounded me on all sides with great showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ laghubhiś citrair brahmāstraparimantritaiḥ vyadhamaṃ sāyakair āśu śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Then I swiftly scattered them with swift and varied arrows consecrated with the Brahmā weapon, by the hundreds and thousands.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpīḍyamānās te krodhāviṣṭā mahāsurāḥ apīḍayan māṃ sahitāḥ śaraśūlāsivṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Then those great asuras, being pressed hard and seized by anger, together tormented me with showers of arrows, spears, and swords.

sanskrit: tato 'ham astram ātiṣṭhaṃ paramaṃ tigmatejasam dayitaṃ devarājasya mādhavaṃ nāma bhārata
english: Then I resorted to the supreme weapon of fierce splendour dear to the king of the gods, named the Mādhava, O Bharata.

sanskrit: tataḥ khaḍgāṃs triśūlāṃś ca tomarāṃś ca sahasraśaḥ astravīryeṇa śatadhā tair muktān aham acchinam
english: Then by the power of that weapon I cut into a hundred pieces the swords, tridents, and spears by the thousands hurled by them.

sanskrit: chittvā praharaṇāny eṣāṃ tatas tān api sarvaśaḥ pratyavidhyam ahaṃ roṣād daśabhir daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Having cut their weapons, I then in anger pierced each and every one of them with ten arrows apiece.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvād dhi tadā saṃkhye yathā bhramarapaṅktayaḥ niṣpatanti tathā bāṇās tan mātalir apūjayat
english: For arrows then issued from the Gāṇḍīva in battle as swarms of bees — Mātali honoured that.

sanskrit: teṣām api tu bāṇās te bahutvāc chalabhā iva avākiran māṃ balavat tān ahaṃ vyadhamaṃ śaraiḥ
english: Their arrows too, like locusts in their multitude, powerfully rained down upon me — I scattered them with my arrows.

sanskrit: vadhyamānās tatas te tu nivātakavacāḥ punaḥ śaravarṣair mahadbhir māṃ samantāt paryavārayan
english: Then those Nivātakavacas, being slaughtered, again surrounded me on all sides with great showers of arrows.
